title: Coca-Cola launches Zero Zero in India; “Zero Caffeine Coke is now available on Zepto,” says Aadit Palicha
summary: Coca-Cola launches Zero Zero caffeine-free cola in India on Zepto
detailed: Coca-Cola has launched its zero-sugar and zero-caffeine cola, Coca-Cola Zero Zero, in India, now available on Zepto, as announced by Aadit Palicha.
Coca-Cola has launched its zero-sugar and zero-caffeine cola, Coca-Cola Zero Zero, in India.

Announcing the development on X on November 27, Aadit Palicha, Co-founder and CEO, Zepto, wrote, “An announcement for all the Coca-Cola lovers, Zero Caffeine Coke is now available on Zepto.”
“It’s selling across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Delhi NCR today - and will be live Pan-India soon!” he added.

sentences: Coca-Cola has launched its zero-sugar and zero-caffeine cola, Coca-Cola Zero Zero, in India, now available on Zepto, as announced by Aadit Palicha.
Coca-Cola has launched its zero-sugar and zero-caffeine cola, Coca-Cola Zero Zero, in India.
The beverage is available through quick commerce platform Zepto.

Announcing the development on X on November 27, Aadit Palicha, Co-founder and CEO, Zepto, wrote, “An announcement for all the Coca-Cola lovers, Zero Caffeine Coke is now available on Zepto.”
“It’s selling across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Delhi NCR today - and will be live Pan-India soon!” he added.
It is a zero-caffeine, zero-sugar and zero-calorie formulation.
In the lead-up to the launch, countdown installations were spotted across Gurugram, Delhi and Mumbai, building anticipation around the new product.
These were followed by the official product reveal, with videos from the launch event subsequently gaining traction on Instagram.

The new variant is aimed at consumers who enjoy cola but prefer to avoid both sugar and caffeine.
By eliminating caffeine, Coca-Cola is also looking to expand consumption occasions, particularly during late evenings and at night, when some consumers may avoid conventional caffeinated soft drinks.
The launch comes at a time when competition in India's low- and no-sugar beverage market is intensifying.
In July, The Economic Times reported that Coca-Cola was planning to bring its globally available caffeine-free cola to India, with production to be undertaken locally.
Industry data cited in the report suggests that low- and zero-sugar beverages now account for 30-35% of soft drink sales, a significant increase from just 5% in 2020.
The caffeine-free offering could also help Coca-Cola tap into late-evening consumption occasions, further expanding its portfolio beyond established products such as Diet Coke and Coke Zero Sugar.
